text:
micah: seeing a weird cluster of client reconnects + 503s for SSE consumers since the canary yesterday. console shows a large number of sessions in "holdoff" state for ~30s then a flurry of reconnects. anyone else?
ben: yup noticed a burst in proxy logs too. looks like our new backpressure holdoff logic is deferring connections and then releasing them in a batch. reproducer: replaying N=200 concurrent streams with sustained token churn.
tara: what console panel are you looking at? sampling might be smoothing the spikes, which would hide the burstiness in the daily view.
micah: Dashboard -> Streaming / Sessions -> session_holdoff_count (1m). link: https://console/redwood/streaming/dashboards/session_holdoff_count (this was in canary region eu-west-1).
ben: config we changed yesterday:
```
proxy.stream_backpressure.enabled = true
proxy.stream_backpressure.holdoff_ms = 30000
proxy.stream_backpressure.release_batch = 500
```
we increased release_batch to allow faster drain but that likely causes the sudden reconnect fanout.
ashley: curious if this causes double billing — if connections are idle in holdoff do we still meter tokens or session minutes?
sre-oncall: holdoff shouldn't count active tokens, but session minutes might be incrementing; need to confirm billing window semantics. tagging @billing-team FYI.
deploy-bot: deploy canary 'stream-backpressure-v2' to eu-west-1 started by @ben at 5420001000 (image: gcr/redwood/stream-backpressure:v2-canary). :rocket:
tara: micah can you post a short log snippet showing the timestamped holdoff release sequence? sampling log lines helps.
micah: paste from proxy logs (trimmed):
```
[5420001012] session=abc123 state=holdoff ms=30012
[5420001032] session=def456 state=holdoff ms=30020
[5420001033] session=ghi789 state=holdoff ms=30021
[5420001050] holdoff_release: releasing batch size=512
[5420001050] connection=abc123 resume OK
[5420001050] connection=def456 resume OK
```
we see the release happening in one tick, so a lot of clients re-open at once.
ben: that's the effect of release_batch. if holdoff windows align, they coalesce. our jitter was too small. current jitter config is 0-50ms, should be larger and maybe exponential backoff for retries.
tara: also console sampling makes the 1m series look like a flat bump; switch to raw 5s timeseries to see real traffic. query suggestion: `sum by (region) (increase(session_holdoff_count[1m]))` for a per-minute spike.
ashley: on billing: if session state = holdoff but transport closed, we might be counting reconnections as new sessions which could inflate minutes. need a safe fallback to mark held sessions as suspended for billing.
sre-oncall: temporary mitigation: rollback canary or set holdoff_ms=5000 and release_batch=50. that will reduce burstiness. I'm reverting canary in eu-west-1 now.
ben: i'll push a small change: add randomized offset up to holdoff_ms * 0.7 to break synchronization, and decrease release_batch default. putting up PR now.
micah: thanks. can we also add a console heatmap for "holdoff_release_latency" so ops can quickly see if releases are clustered?
console-bot: new panel suggestion posted: https://console/redwood/streaming/panels/holdoff-heatmap (draft).
tara: follow-ups: (1) widen jitter and make it proportional to session age, (2) add metric for queued_count and queued_release_batch_size, (3) confirm billing semantics with finance.
ashley: i'll own the billing check. assigning to myself.
sre-oncall: plan: rollback canary in eu-west-1 (done), patch jitter + batch defaults, test at 200 concurrent streams, then re-canary. will update here when staged.
micah: confirmed rollback reduced 503 spike immediately. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
ben: PR: https://git/repo/pulls/412 (patch + tests). will schedule canary mid-day after QA run.
micah: leaving this thread open until canary is healthy in eu-west-1.
